motivation: Active TX queue receive must not wait for an ingress producer paused mid-enqueue. This is not an established diagnosis of the preserved historical RF queue faults.
consumer: try_lock once; contention returns temporary Empty, never Full/Disconnected and never discards/restamps a message. Exactly one non-Sync receiver.
producer: Serialized, preallocated deque push; no I/O, sample processing, formatting, callbacks or payload destruction under the production lock. Producer enqueue can wait for its short queue mutex; it is not a wait-free producer API. Owner-local bootstrap enqueues only before RF.
capacity: Unchanged: commands 16, audio 16, feedback FEEDBACK_QUEUE_BLOCKS=16. Existing original-age watchdogs, overload policy, output fences and fault latch unchanged.
regressions: Last sender closes only after pending messages drain
Paused producer cannot hold consumer receive
Receiver close during paused enqueue rejects original envelope
Actual scheduled owner release/stop receipt/native cleanup while production feedback queue producer stays paused
nativeIntegration: PS-off two-tone through actual run_inner, both backend fixtures
Auto release/re-arm through actual run_inner, both backend fixtures
Sustained Auto, two 15-second generations per backend, actual run_inner, real WDSP
limits: No new ARM execution or live RF yet for this candidate.
This bounds consumer queue acquisition only; it does not claim the entire TX call graph is wait-free.
